newsitem.title: FRANCE: French left leads centre-right in poll projections.
newsitem.headline: French left leads centre-right in poll projections.

text.p: The combined left strongly outpolled the ruling centre-right coalition in the first round of France's parliamentary election on Sunday, all polling institutes said.

Projections televised as soon as polling stations closed at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT) suggested the electorate had cast a huge protest vote against Prime Minister Alain Juppe's conservative government after two years of austerity and rising unemployment and the outcome of next Sunday's runoff round was wide open.

The Socialists, Communists, extreme-left and other left-wing candidates were forecast to capture between 40.6 and 41.6 percent of the vote, with the ruling RPR-UDF coalition and other moderate right candidates scoring between 36.1 and 37.1 percent.
The extreme-right National Front was projected to win between 14.8 and 15.1 percent, its strongest showing in a parliamentary election.

Most of the 577 National Assembly seats were expected to go to a runoff next Sunday, where the behaviour of National Front voters and of the roughly 32 percent of voters who abstained on the first round will be crucial.
